q: (only Allaah knows the best correct meaning of these letters).
v.s: Tā, Hā.
v.c: Ṭâ-Hâ.

q: We have not revealed the Qur'aan to you to cause you difficulty
(you should therefore not make its teachings difficult for yourself).
v.s: We have not sent down to you the Qur’ān that you be distressed
v.c: We have not revealed the Quran to you ˹O Prophet˺ to cause you distress,

q: is advice for him who fears
v.s: But only as a reminder for those who fear [God] -
v.c: but as a reminder to those in awe ˹of Allah˺.

q: A revelation from Him Who created the earth and the lofty skies.
v.s: A revelation from He who created the earth and highest heavens,
v.c: ˹It is˺ a revelation from the One Who created the earth and the high heavens—

q: Ar Rahmaan is firmly in control of the Throne.
(None has any share in His kingdom.)
v.s: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established.
v.c: the Most Compassionate, ˹Who is˺ established on the Throne.

q: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens, whatever is on the earth, whatever is between the two, and whatever is beneath the clay.
v.s: To Him belongs what is in the heavens and what is on the earth and what is between them and what is under the soil.
v.c: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is in between and whatever is underground.

q: (it makes no difference to Him because)
He knows what is whispered and all that is even more hidden
(such as the unspoken thoughts and desires of the heart).
v.s: And if you speak aloud - then indeed, He knows the secret and what is [even] more hidden.
v.c: Whether you speak openly ˹or not˺, He certainly knows what is secret and what is even more hidden.

q: Allaah is such that there is no Ilaah but He. His
v.s: God - there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the best names.
v.c: Allah—there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. He has the Most Beautiful Names.

q: Has not the story of Moosa ﵊ reached you?
v.s: And has the story of Moses reached you? -
v.c: Has the story of Moses reached you ˹O Prophet˺?

q: (as he proceeded from Madyan to Egypt and was lost,)
a fire and said to his wife, “Wait
(to give us some light and heat),
or I may find some guide at the fire.”
v.s: When he saw a fire and said to his family, "Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire; perhaps I can bring you a torch or find at the fire some guidance."
v.c: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, “Wait here, ˹for˺ I have spotted a fire. Perhaps I can bring you a torch from it, or find some guidance at the fire.”

v.s: And when he came to it, he was called, "O Moses,
v.c: But when he approached it, he was called, “O Moses!

q: “I am indeed your Rabb, so remove your shoes for you are on the holy plain of Tuwa.”
v.s: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwā.
v.c: It is truly I. I am your Lord! So take off your sandals, for you are in the sacred valley of Ṭuwa.

q: so listen attentively to what is being revealed.”
v.s: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed [to you].
v.c: I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed:

q: “Verily I am Allaah. There is no Ilaah but Me, so worship Me and establish salaah for My remembrance.”
v.s: Indeed, I am God. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
v.c: ‘It is truly I. I am Allah! There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Me. So worship Me ˹alone˺, and establish prayer for My remembrance.

q: “Qiyaamah is undoubtedly coming. I shall conceal
(will come. Qiyaamah will have to come)
so that every soul can be granted retribution
v.s: Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives.
v.c: The Hour is sure to come. My Will is to keep it hidden, so that every soul may be rewarded according to their efforts.

q: “The person who does not believe in it and who follows his carnal passions should never prevent
(from believing in Qiyaamah and from performing salaah),
(for being a Kaafir and a sinner).'
v.s: So do not let one avert you from it who does not believe in it and follows his desire, for you [then] would perish.
v.c: So do not let those who disbelieve in it and follow their desires distract you from it, or you will be doomed.’”

q: “What is that in your right hand, O Moosa?”(
This made him fully aware of it.)
v.s: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?"
v.c: ˹Allah added,˺ “And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?”

q: use it to beat down leaves for my goats
I have many other uses for it.”
v.s: He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I bring down leaves for my sheep and I have therein other uses."
v.c: He replied, “It is my staff! I lean on it, and with it I beat down ˹branches˺ for my sheep, and have other uses for it.”

q: Allaah said, “Throw it down, O Moosa.”
v.s: [God] said, "Throw it down, O Moses."
v.c: Allah said, “Throw it down, O Moses!”

q: So he threw it down, and suddenly it was a slithering
v.s: So he threw it down, and thereupon it was a snake, moving swiftly.
v.c: So he did, then—behold!—it became a serpent, slithering.

q: Allaah said, “Grab hold of it and do not be afraid. We shall soon return it to its former
(When Moosa ﵊ grabbed hold of the snake, it became a staff once again.)
v.s: [God] said, "Seize it and fear not; We will return it to its former condition.
v.c: Allah said, “Take it, and have no fear. We will return it to its former state.

q: (a second miracle which you may show to people to prove that you are My Rasool).”
v.s: And draw in your hand to your side; it will come out white without disease - another sign,
v.c: And put your hand under your armpit, it will come out ˹shining˺ white, unblemished, as another sign,

q: “(We have demonstrated these miracles to you)
So that We may show you some of Our magnificent
(so that you can be convinced of My power and preach it to others).”
v.s: That We may show you [some] of Our greater signs.
v.c: so that We may show you some of Our greatest signs.

q: (and preach Towheed to him and his people).
v.s: Go to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed [i.e., tyrannized]."
v.c: Go to Pharaoh, for he has truly transgressed ˹all bounds˺.”

q: (Realising that the task was a great one,)
(to be able to bear Your message and to have the courage to propagate it)...”
v.s: [Moses] said, "My Lord, expand [i.e., relax] for me my breast [with assurance]
v.c: Moses prayed, “My Lord! Uplift my heart for me,

v.s: And ease for me my task
v.c: and make my task easy,

v.s: And untie the knot from my tongue
v.c: and remove the impediment from my tongue

v.s: That they may understand my speech.
v.c: so people may understand my speech,

v.s: And appoint for me a minister [i.e., assistant] from my family -
v.c: and grant me a helper from my family,

v.s: Aaron, my brother.
v.c: Aaron, my brother.

v.s: Increase through him my strength
v.c: Strengthen me through him,

q: “...and make him a partner to my task
v.s: And let him share my task
v.c: and let him share my task,

v.s: That we may exalt You much
v.c: so that we may glorify You much

q: (because it is easier to achieve something when the responsibility is shared).”
v.s: And remember You much.
v.c: and remember You much,

q: “Undoubtedly You are Ever Watchful over us
v.s: Indeed, You are of us ever Seeing."
v.c: for truly You have ˹always˺ been overseeing us.”

q: Allaah said, “You have been granted your request O Moosa
(We shall make your task easy and appoint Haaroon ﵊ as a Nabi to assist you).”
v.s: [God] said, "You have been granted your request, O Moses.
v.c: Allah responded, “All that you requested has been granted, O Moses!

q: “(We will favour you today just as)
favours upon you on another occasion...”
v.s: And We had already conferred favor upon you another time,
v.c: “And surely We had shown You favour before,

q: We inspired your mother with that with which she was inspired.”
v.s: When We inspired to your mother what We inspired,
v.c: when We inspired your mother with this:

m: and that you may be brought up
q: and then cast the box into the river
(Nile, because Fir'oun's soldiers were ordered to kill all little boys born to the Bani Israa'eel).
The river will wash him on to the bank when My
(enveloped you with love so that Fir'oun and whoever else saw you began loving you)
so that you may grow up under My supervision
(care and protection).” (Fir'oun's wife the queen then persuaded him to allow her to keep the child as her own son. See verse 6-12 of Surah 28.)
v.s: [Saying], 'Cast him into the chest and cast it into the river, and the river will throw it onto the bank; there will take him an enemy to Me and an enemy to him.' And I bestowed upon you love from Me that you would be brought up under My eye [i.e., observation and care].
v.c: ‘Put him into a chest, then put it into the river. The river will wash it ashore, and he will be taken by ˹Pharaoh,˺ an enemy of Mine and his.’ And I blessed you with lovability from Me ˹O Moses˺ so that you would be brought up under My ˹watchful˺ Eye.

q: (after seeing that the little baby Moosa ﵊ refused to drink milk from any nursing mother, she pretended to be a bystander and)
she said, 'Should I not show you someone who can
(Desperate to find someone, Fir'oun's wife allowed Moosa ﵊ sister to indicate Moosa ﵊ mother. The child naturally took to the mother to the relief of the queen.)
We returned you to your mother so that her eyes may be cooled
and We saved you from grief
and tried you with many trials
years with the people of Madyan
and then, O Moosa, you have arrived
(at the age when I wish to form ally proclaim your Risaalah).”
v.s: [And We favored you] when your sister went and said, 'Shall I direct you to someone who will be responsible for him?' So We restored you to your mother that she might be content and not grieve. And you killed someone, but We saved you from retaliation and tried you with a [severe] trial. And you remained [some] years among the people of Madyan. Then you came [here] at the decreed time, O Moses.
v.c: ˹Remember˺ when your sister came along and proposed, ‘Shall I direct you to someone who will nurse him?’ So We reunited you with your mother so that her heart would be put at ease, and she would not grieve. ˹Later˺ you killed a man ˹by mistake˺, but We saved you from sorrow, as well as other tests We put you through. Then you stayed for a number of years among the people of Midian. Then you came here as pre-destined, O Moses!

v.s: And I produced you for Myself.
v.c: And I have selected you for My service.

v.s: Go, you and your brother, with My signs and do not slacken in My remembrance.
v.c: “Go forth, you and your brother, with My signs and never falter in remembering Me.

q: “Proceed, the two of you, to Fir'oun. Indeed he is rebellious.”
v.s: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
v.c: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh, for he has truly transgressed ˹all bounds˺.

q: words, perchance he may take heed or fear
v.s: And speak to him with gentle speech that perhaps he may be reminded or fear [God]."
v.c: Speak to him gently, so perhaps he may be mindful ˹of Me˺ or fearful ˹of My punishment˺.”

q: They said, “O our Rabb! We truly fear that he would be defiant or rebel against us.”
v.s: They said, "Our Lord, indeed we are afraid that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress."
v.c: They both pleaded, “Our Lord! We fear that he may be quick to harm us or act tyrannically.”

q: Allaah said, “Have no fear, for verily I am with you, hearing and seeing
(I am with you to protect you wherever you are).'
v.s: [God] said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see.
v.c: Allah reassured ˹them˺, “Have no fear! I am with you, hearing and seeing.

q: “Go to him and say, 'We are indeed two Rasools of our Rabb, so send the Bani Israa'eel with us
and do not torture them. We have come to you with a sure Aayah
ay peace be on those who follow the guidance
(who accept totally the message we have brought).'”
v.s: So go to him and say, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord, so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And peace will be upon he who follows the guidance.
v.c: So go to him and say, ‘Indeed we are both messengers from your Lord, so let the Children of Israel go with us, and do not oppress them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord. And salvation will be for whoever follows the ˹right˺ guidance.

q: “It has been revealed to us that punishment shall
v.s: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.'"
v.c: It has indeed been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies ˹the truth˺ and turns away.’”

q: (As commanded, Moosa ﵊ and Haaroon ﵊ took the message to Fir'oun. However, he rejected their message.)
Fir'oun said, “Then who is the Rabb of you two, O Moosa?”
v.s: [Pharaoh] said, "So who is the Lord of you two, O Moses?"
v.c: Pharaoh asked, “Who then is the Lord of you two, O Moses?”

q: replied, “Our Rabb is He Who granted each thing its
(showed it what it ought to be doing and how to live).”
v.s: He said, "Our Lord is He who gave each thing its form and then guided [it]."
v.c: He answered, “Our Lord is the One Who has given everything its ˹distinctive˺ form, then guided ˹it˺.”

q: Fir'oun said, “Then what about the previous generations
(who rejected the message of their. Were they also punished as you say)?”
v.s: [Pharaoh] said, "Then what is the case of the former generations?"
v.c: Pharaoh asked, “And what about previous peoples?”

q: Moosa ﵊ said, “The knowledge of them is with my Rabb in the Book
My Rabb does not err, nor does He forget.”

(He knows whether a nation deserves punishment in this world before their punishment in the Aakhirah. While many nations were punished in this world, the punishment for others has been postponed for the Aakhirah.)
v.s: [Moses] said, "The knowledge thereof is with my Lord in a record. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."
v.c: He replied, “That knowledge is with my Lord in a Record. My Lord neither falters nor forgets ˹anything˺.”

q: He Who made the earth a bedding
for you, made roads for you
and sent water from the sky.” Then We extracted
various kinds of plants for you.
v.s: [It is He] who has made for you the earth as a bed [spread out] and inserted therein for you roadways and sent down from the sky, rain and produced thereby categories of various plants.
v.c: ˹He is the One˺ Who has laid out the earth for ˹all of˺ you, and set in it pathways for you, and sends down rain from the sky, causing various types of plants to grow,

v.s: Eat [therefrom] and pasture your livestock. Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.
v.c: ˹so˺ eat and graze your cattle. Surely in this are signs for people of sound judgment.

q: you from it a second time
(when you will all come out from your graves on the Day of Qiyaamah).
v.s: From it [i.e., the earth] We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will extract you another time.
v.c: From the earth We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you back again.

q: Verily We showed Fir'oun all Our Aayaat, yet he
v.s: And We certainly showed him [i.e., Pharaoh] Our signs - all of them - but he denied and refused.
v.c: And We certainly showed Pharaoh all of Our signs, but he denied them and refused ˹to believe˺.

q: (Referring to the miracles that Moosa ﵊ showed him,)
said, “Have you come to us to remove us from our land with your magic
v.s: He said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?
v.c: He said, “Have you come to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?

m: Then we will surely produce for you
q: (Intending to host a contest between Moosa ﵊ and all the accomplished magicians of Egypt, Fir'oun said to Moosa ﵊,)
we will certainly present the same kind of magic before you, so arrange an appointment between us that neither us nor you will violate. Fix an open plain for this
(contest so that people may witness it).”
v.s: Then we will surely bring you magic like it, so make between us and you an appointment, which we will not fail to keep and neither will you, in a place assigned."
v.c: We can surely meet you with similar magic. So set for us an appointment that neither of us will fail to keep, in a central place.”

q: shall be on the day of adornment
(a day of festivity to celebrate Firoun's birth day),
and the people should be gathered at midmorning
v.s: [Moses] said, "Your appointment is on the day of the festival when the people assemble at mid-morning."
v.c: Moses said, “Your appointment is on the Day of the Festival, and let the people be gathered mid-morning.”

q: (to face Moosa ﵊ on the appointed day after extensive preparation, some say after a year of preparation).
v.s: So Pharaoh went away, put together his plan, and then came [to Moses].
v.c: Pharaoh then withdrew, orchestrated his scheme, then returned.

q: “Woe be to you! Do not invent lies against Allaah
(by claiming that others are His partners),
for then He will destroy you with a
(in both worlds and will never achieve the good).”
v.s: Moses said to them [i.e., the magicians summoned by Pharaoh], "Woe to you! Do not invent a lie against God or He will exterminate you with a punishment; and he has failed who invents [such falsehood]."
v.c: Moses warned the magicians, “Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah, or He will wipe you out with a torment. Whoever fabricates ˹lies˺ is bound to fail.”

q: the issue between themselves and then secretly convened
v.s: So they disputed over their affair among themselves and concealed their private conversation.
v.c: So the magicians disputed the matter among themselves, conversing privately.

q: are but two magicians who want to remove you from your land with their magic and destroy your excellent ways.”
v.s: They said, "Indeed, these are two magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic and do away with your most exemplary way [i.e., religion or tradition].
v.c: They concluded, “These two are only magicians who want to drive you out of your land with their magic, and do away with your most cherished traditions.

q: “So assemble your plans and present yourselves in rows. The one who is victorious
v.s: So resolve upon your plan and then come [forward] in line. And he has succeeded today who overcomes."
v.c: So orchestrate your plan, then come forward in ˹perfect˺ ranks. And whoever prevails today will certainly be successful.”

q: They said, “O Moosa! Either you throw
or should we be the first to throw
v.s: They said, "O Moses, either you throw or we will be the first to throw."
v.c: They said, “O Moses! Either you cast, or let us be the first to cast.”

q: suddenly seemed to appear like slithering
(The magicians merely made everyone think that there were snakes whereas these were only illusions.)
v.s: He said, "Rather, you throw." And suddenly their ropes and staffs seemed to him from their magic that they were moving [like snakes].
v.c: Moses responded, “No, you go first.” And suddenly their ropes and staffs appeared to him—by their magic—to be slithering.

q: So Moosa ﵊ sensed a bit of fear in his heart
(fearing that the people may become confused and think that the magicians are also capable of performing miracles like himself).
v.s: And he sensed within himself apprehension, did Moses.
v.c: So Moses concealed fear within himself.

q: We said, “Do not fear! You shall definitely remain high
v.s: We [i.e., God] said, "Fear not. Indeed, it is you who are superior.
v.c: We reassured ˹him˺, “Do not fear! It is certainly you who will prevail.

q: “Throw down what is in your right hand and it will devour
what they have faked. They have merely faked the plot of a magician, and a magician will never succeed
(As instructed, Moosa ﵊ threw down his staff which ate up all the snakes of the magicians.)
v.s: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have crafted. What they have crafted is but the trick of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is."
v.c: Cast what is in your right hand, and it will swallow up what they have made, for what they have made is no more than a magic trick. And magicians can never succeed wherever they go.”

q: (seeing that the snake of Moosa ﵊' was not a fake like theirs,)
(astounded and realising that he must surely be Allaah's Rasool, they were)
saying, “We believe in the Rabb of Haaroon and Moosa.”
v.s: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."
v.c: So the magicians fell down in prostration, declaring, “We believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses.”

m: So surely I will cut off
and surely I will crucify you
q: Fir'oun said, “Do you believe in Moosa before I have permitted you
who has taught you magic. I shall certainly cut off your hands and your legs on opposite sides and will surely crucify you
on the trunks of date palms. Then you will learn which of us
is more severe in punishment and whose punishment is more lingering
v.s: [Pharaoh] said, "You believed him [i.e., Moses] before I gave you permission. Indeed, he is your leader who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [giving] punishment and more enduring."
v.c: Pharaoh threatened, “How dare you believe in him before I give you permission? He must be your master who taught you magic. I will certainly cut off your hands and feet on opposite sides, and crucify you on the trunks of palm trees. You will really see whose punishment is more severe and more lasting.”

q: replied, “We shall never prefer you to the clear signs that have come to us and to the One Who has created us. So do as you decide. You can make a decision only in this worldly life
(you can end our lives only in this world and have no control over our lives in the Aakhirah, when Allaah will grant us Jannah).”
v.s: They said, "Never will we prefer you over what has come to us of clear proofs and [over] He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree for this worldly life.
v.c: They responded, “By the One Who created us! We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us. So do whatever you want! Your authority only covers the ˹fleeting˺ life of this world.

q: “We have verily believed in our Rabb so that He may forgive us for our sins and for the magic that you have forced
us to practise. Allaah is Best and Eternal.”
v.s: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us [to do] of magic. And God is better and more enduring."
v.c: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord so He may forgive our sins and that magic you have forced us to practice. And Allah is far superior ˹in reward˺ and more lasting ˹in punishment˺.”

q: Indeed whoever comes to his Rabb as a criminal
then he shall have Jahannam where he shall neither live
(because there is no death in the Aakhirah).
v.s: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - indeed, for him is Hell; he will neither die therein nor live.
v.c: Whoever comes to their Lord as an evildoer will certainly have Hell, where they can neither live nor die.

q: As for him who comes to his Rabb as a Mu'min, having performed good acts
then these people will have the lofty ranks
v.s: But whoever comes to Him as a believer having done righteous deeds - for those will be the highest degrees [in position]:
v.c: But whoever comes to Him as a believer, having done good, they will have the highest ranks:

q: The eternal Jannaat beneath which rivers flow. There they shall live forever. This is the reward for those who are pure
(who purify their inner selves from all types of evil).
v.s: Gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally. And that is the reward of one who purifies himself.
v.c: the Gardens of Eternity, under which rivers flow, where they will stay forever. That is the reward of those who purify themselves.

q: We certainly sent revelation to Moosa ﵊
(when they reach the sea, strike your staff on the sea to)
make for them a dry road in the sea. Neither should you fear anyone pursuing you, nor should you have any other fear.”
(Consequently, when Moosa ﵊ struck the sea with his staff and Allaah opened twelve roads within the sea for them to cross, Fir'oun decided to give chase.)
v.s: And We had inspired to Moses, "Travel by night with My servants and strike for them a dry path through the sea; you will not fear being overtaken [by Pharaoh] nor be afraid [of drowning]."
v.c: And We surely inspired Moses, ˹saying,˺ “Leave with My servants ˹at night˺ and strike a dry passage for them across the sea. Have no fear of being overtaken, nor be concerned ˹of drowning˺.”

q: So Fir'oun followed them with his army
v.s: So Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them,
v.c: Then Pharaoh pursued them with his soldiers—but how overwhelming were the waters that submerged them!

q: his nation and did not guide them.
v.s: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide [them].
v.c: And ˹so˺ Pharaoh led his people astray, and did not guide ˹them rightly˺.

m: and We made a covenant with you
q: O Bani Israa'eel! We have certainly rescued
you from your enemy, made an appointment
at the right side of Mount Toor
and sent for you Manna and Salwa
(when you were wandering lost in the Valley of Teeh).
v.s: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mount, and We sent down to you manna and quails,
v.c: O Children of Israel! We saved you from your enemy, and made an appointment with you on the right side of Mount Ṭûr, and sent down to you manna and quails,

q: Eat from the pure things that We have provided for you and do not transgress
(by disobeying the commands of the One Who gave you all these favours),
shall descend on you. The one upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen
(from My esteem and into the fire of Jahannam).
v.s: [Saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you and do not transgress [or oppress others] therein, lest My anger should descend upon you. And he upon whom My anger descends has certainly fallen [i.e., perished]."
v.c: ˹saying,˺ “Eat from the good things We have provided for you, but do not transgress in them, or My wrath will befall you. And whoever My wrath befalls is certainly doomed.

q: I am certainly the Most Forgiving towards the one who repents
(remains steadfast on Imaan and continues to carry out good actions until death).
v.s: But indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of whoever repents and believes and does righteousness and then continues in guidance.
v.c: But I am truly Most Forgiving to whoever repents, believes, and does good, then persists on ˹true˺ guidance.”

q: (In his eagerness to receive the Torah from Allaah at Mount Toor, Moosa ﵊ hurried ahead of some people who were supposed to accompany him there, causing them to remain behind with the rest of the people who eventually were involved in worshipping the calf. It was with reference to this that Allaah asked him,)
“What has made you hasten ahead of your people, O Moosa?”
v.s: [God said], "And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?"
v.c: ˹Allah asked,˺ “Why have you come with such haste ahead of your people, O Moses?”

q: He replied, “They are on my track
I have hastened to You, O my Rabb, so that You may be pleased
v.s: He said, "They are close upon my tracks, and I hastened to You, my Lord, that You be pleased."
v.c: He replied, “They are close on my tracks. And I have hastened to You, my Lord, so You will be pleased.”

q: and Saamiri has led them astray
(by making the golden calf and encouraging them to worship it).'
v.s: [God] said, "But indeed, We have tried your people after you [departed], and the Sāmirī has led them astray."
v.c: Allah responded, “We have indeed tested your people in your absence, and the Sâmiri has led them astray.”

q: Moosa ﵊ returned to his people in anger and remorse. He said, “O my people! Has your Rabb not made you a fair promise
(that He will send you a Book containing the injunctions of your Deen)?
Has too much time elapsed for you
(causing you to think that you will never receive the Book and that you may as well worship something else)
or did you wish that the anger of your Rabb should descend on you, because of which you broke the promise
(the promise not to do anything against the Shari'ah while I am away and to obey?”)
v.s: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, "O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Then, was the time [of its fulfillment] too long for you, or did you wish that wrath from your Lord descend upon you, so you broke your promise [of obedience] to me?"
v.c: So Moses returned to his people, furious and sorrowful. He said, “O my people! Had your Lord not made you a good promise? Has my absence been too long for you? Or have you wished for wrath from your Lord to befall you, so you broke your promise to me?”

q: said, “We have not broken the promise
made with you of our own accord, but we were laden with the burdens of a nation
(we were carrying jewellery belonging to the people of Fir'oun, which they lent to us)
(the mould of the calf and then threw the sand from footprints of Jibra'eel ﵊ horse into it, causing the calf to make sounds).”
v.s: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our will, but we were made to carry burdens from the ornaments of the people [of Pharaoh], so we threw them [into the fire], and thus did the Sāmirī throw."
v.c: They argued, “We did not break our promise to you of our own free will, but we were made to carry the burden of the people’s ˹golden˺ jewellery, then we threw it ˹into the fire˺, and so did the Sâmiri.”

q: made for them a calf that was a body which made the sounds of a cow. They
“This is your Rabb and the Rabb of Moosa, but he
(that his Rabb is here and has gone to the mountain to look for it).”
v.s: And he extracted for them [the statue of] a calf which had a lowing sound, and they said, "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot."
v.c: Then he moulded for them an idol of a calf that made a lowing sound. They said, “This is your god and the god of Moses, but Moses forgot ˹where it was˺!”

q: could not reply to them nor did it possess the ability to benefit or harm them?
(How could it therefore be their god?)
v.s: Did they not see that it could not return to them any speech [i.e., response] and that it did not possess for them any harm or benefit?
v.c: Did they not see that it did not respond to them, nor could it protect or benefit them?

q: “O my people! You are merely being tested
Without doubt, your Rabb is Ar Rahmaan
so follow me and obey my command
v.s: And Aaron had already told them before [the return of Moses], "O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order."
v.c: Aaron had already warned them beforehand, “O my people! You are only being tested by this, for indeed your ˹one true˺ Lord is the Most Compassionate. So follow me and obey my orders.”

q: They replied, “We shall certainly remain devoted to it until Moosa ﵊ returns to us
v.s: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to it [i.e., the calf] until Moses returns to us."
v.c: They replied, “We will not cease to worship it until Moses returns to us.”

q: Moosa ﵊ said, “O Haaroon! When you saw them going astray, what prevented you...”
v.s: [Moses] said, "O Aaron, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray,
v.c: Moses scolded ˹his brother˺, “O Aaron! What prevented you, when you saw them going astray,

q: (to the mountain, thereby disassociating from them so that they could realise that you truly detested their actions)?
(referring to the instruction mentioned in verse 142 of Surah 7, which reads:”.. .do not follow the path of those who cause corruption)’’.
v.s: From following me? Then have you disobeyed my order?"
v.c: from following after me? How could you disobey my orders?”

q: Haaroon ﵊ said, “O son of my mother! Do not grab my beard or
I feared that you would say, 'You divided the Bani Israa'eel and did not wait for my word
v.s: [Aaron] said, "O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or by my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, 'You caused division among the Children of Israel, and you did not observe [or await] my word.'"
v.c: Aaron pleaded, “O son of my mother! Do not seize me by my beard or ˹the hair of˺ my head. I really feared that you would say, ‘You have caused division among the Children of Israel, and did not observe my word.’”

q: said, “What have you to say, O Saamiri?”
v.s: [Moses] said, "And what is your case, O Sāmirī?"
v.c: Moses then asked, “What did you think you were doing, O Sâmiri?”

q: replied, “I saw what they did not see

(When Saamiri saw Jibra'eel ﵊ he noticed that greenery sprouted from every portion of land on which Jibra'eel ﵊ horse stepped. This made him realise that its footsteps must contain some wonderful powers, which he could use in the calf.)
v.s: He said, "I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful [of dust] from the track of the messenger and threw it, and thus did my soul entice me."
v.c: He said, “I saw what they did not see, so I took a handful ˹of dust˺ from the hoof-prints of ˹the horse of˺ the messenger-angel ˹Gabriel˺ then cast it ˹on the moulded calf˺. This is what my lower-self tempted me into.”

q: Your punishment in this world shall be that you wander around saying, 'Do not touch!'

(Allaah made it such that whenever someone touched Saamiri, or he touched anyone, both persons would be immediately affected by severe fever. Therefore, people stayed far from him and he vehemently avoided them.)
that you cannot miss. Look at your Ilaah
to which you remained so devoted. We will surely burn it and then
(until no trace of it is left).”
v.s: [Moses] said, "Then go. And indeed, it is [decreed] for you in [this] life to say, 'No contact.' And indeed, you have an appointment [in the Hereafter] you will not fail to keep. And look at your 'god' to which you remained devoted. We will surely burn it and blow it [i.e., its ashes] into the sea with a blast.
v.c: Moses said, “Go away then! And for ˹the rest of your˺ life you will surely be crying, ‘Do not touch ˹me˺!’ Then you will certainly have a fate that you cannot escape. Now look at your god to which you have been devoted: we will burn it up, then scatter it in the sea completely.”

q: Your Ilaah is only Allaah, besides Whom there is no other Ilaah. His knowledge encompasses everything.
v.s: Your god is only God, except for whom there is no deity. He has encompassed all things in knowledge."
v.c: ˹Then Moses addressed his people,˺ “Your only god is Allah, there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. He encompasses everything in ˹His˺ knowledge.”

q: (as We have narrated to you the story of Moosa ﵊)
do We narrate to you some of the incidents
that have passed. We have certainly given you advice
v.s: Thus, [O Muhammad], We relate to you from the news of what has preceded. And We have certainly given you from Us a message [i.e., the Qur’ān.]
v.c: This is how We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ some of the stories of the past. And We have certainly granted you a Reminder from Us.

q: (the Qur'aan by refusing to believe that it is from Allaah)
v.s: Whoever turns away from it - then indeed, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden [i.e., great sin],
v.c: Whoever turns away from it will surely bear the burden ˹of sin˺ on the Day of Judgment,

q: forever. It shall be a terrible burden indeed for them on the Day of Qiyaamah
(because it will lead them to Jahannam).
v.s: [Abiding] eternally therein, and evil it is for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load -
v.c: suffering its consequences forever. What an evil burden they will carry on Judgment Day!

q: The day when the trumpet will be blown and the criminals
v.s: The Day the Horn will be blown. And We will gather the criminals, that Day, blue-eyed.
v.c: ˹Beware of˺ the Day the Trumpet will be blown, and We will gather the wicked on that Day blue-faced ˹from horror and thirst˺.

q: (Because of the length of the Day of Qiyaamah,)
They will whisper to each other saying, “You have stayed
v.s: They will murmur among themselves, "You remained not but ten [days in the world]."
v.c: They will whisper among themselves, “You stayed no more than ten days ˹on the earth˺.”

q: We know best what they will speak
(because We have knowledge of the future),
when the most sensible one of them will say, “You had stayed
v.s: We are most knowing of what they say when the best of them in manner [i.e., wisdom or speech] will say, "You remained not but one day."
v.c: We know best what they will say—the most reasonable of them will say, “You stayed no more than a day.”

q: (what will happen to the mountains on the Day of Qiyaamah?).
Say, “My Rabb shall completely remove them
v.s: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, "My Lord will blow them away with a blast.
v.c: And ˹if˺ they ask you ˹O Prophet˺ about the mountains, ˹then˺ say, “My Lord will wipe them out completely,

v.s: And He will leave it [i.e., the earth] a level plain;
v.c: leaving the earth level and bare,

q: “...on which you will neither see any depressions nor any protrusions
(with nothing sunken below or standing above the ground).'
v.s: You will not see therein a depression or an elevation."
v.c: with neither depressions nor elevations to be seen.”

q: (the people after rising from their graves)
(without moving to the right or left).
Voices will be lowered before Ar Rahmaan
you will hear only the sound of footsteps
(as people proceed towards the Plain of Resurrection).
v.s: That Day, they [i.e., everyone] will follow [the call of] the Caller [with] no deviation therefrom, and [all] voices will be stilled before the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper [of footsteps].
v.c: On that Day all will follow the caller ˹for assembly˺, ˹and˺ none will dare to deviate. All voices will be hushed before the Most Compassionate. Only whispers will be heard.

q: On that day intercession will benefit only those whom Ar Rahmaan permits and those with whose speech He is well pleased.
(Only those whom Allaah allows to intercede will be able to do so and they will be allowed to intercede only for those on whose behalf Allaah allows them to intercede.)
v.s: That Day, no intercession will benefit except [that of] one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and has accepted his word.
v.c: On that Day no intercession will be of any benefit, except by those granted permission by the Most Compassionate and whose words are agreeable to Him.

q: He knows what is before them
while they are unable to encompass
(they will never be able to know all that Allaah knows).
v.s: He [i.e., God] knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, but they do not encompass it [i.e., what He knows] in knowledge.
v.c: He ˹fully˺ knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them, but they cannot encompass Him in ˹their˺ knowledge.

q: will certainly be at a loss.
v.s: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. And he will have failed who carries injustice.
v.c: And all faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, All-Sustaining. And those burdened with wrongdoing will be in loss.

q: Whoever carried out good acts as a Mu'min will not have to fear any oppression
(he will not be punished for sins he did not commit),
v.s: But he who does of righteous deeds while he is a believer - he will neither fear injustice nor deprivation.
v.c: But whoever does good and is a believer will have no fear of being wronged or denied ˹their reward˺.

q: as an Arabic Qur'aan and explained various warnings in it so that they fear
or so that it creates some type of understanding
v.s: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur’ān and have diversified therein the warnings that perhaps they will avoid [sin] or it would cause them remembrance.
v.c: And so We have sent it down as an Arabic Quran and varied the warnings in it, so perhaps they will shun evil or it may cause them to be mindful.

q: Exalted is Allaah, the True King.
Do not be hasty with the Qur'aan
(do not try to repeat the verses of the Qur'aan)
before its revelation is completed to you
(wait for Jibra'eel ﵊ to recite the complete verses to you before attempting to repeat them).
(praying to Allaah to allow you to remember all of it,)
say “O my Rabb! Increase my knowledge.”
v.s: So high [above all] is God, the Sovereign, the Truth. And, [O Muhammad], do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur’ān before its revelation is completed to you, and say, “My Lord, increase me in knowledge.”
v.c: Exalted is Allah, the True King! Do not rush to recite ˹a revelation of˺ the Quran ˹O Prophet˺ before it is ˹properly˺ conveyed to you, and pray, “My Lord! Increase me in knowledge.”

q: (not to eat from a particular tree)
before, but he forgot and We did not find him to be determined
(to remember what We had told him).
v.s: And We had already taken a promise from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him determination.
v.c: And indeed, We once made a covenant with Adam, but he forgot, and ˹so˺ We did not find determination in him.

q: When We told the angels, “Prostrate before Aadam,” so they all prostrated, except Iblees. He refused
v.s: And [mention] when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except Iblees; he refused.
v.c: And ˹remember˺ when We said to the angels, “Prostrate before Adam,” so they all did—but not Iblîs, who refused ˹arrogantly˺.

q: So We said, “O Aadam! Indeed he
enemy to you and your wife, so he should never remove the two of you from Jannah
(by being deprived of the bounties that are here).”
v.s: So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. Then let him not remove you from Paradise so you would suffer.
v.c: So We cautioned, “O Adam! This is surely an enemy to you and to your wife. So do not let him drive you both out of Paradise, for you ˹O Adam˺ would then suffer ˹hardship˺.

q: “Without doubt you shall never be hungry nor naked here
v.s: Indeed, it is [promised] for you not to be hungry therein or be unclothed.
v.c: Here it is guaranteed that you will never go hungry or unclothed,

q: “You will never be thirsty here, nor will you be exposed to sunlight.
“(Food, drink, dress,, shelter are essential requirements for man.)
v.s: And indeed, you will not be thirsty therein or be hot from the sun."
v.c: nor will you ˹ever˺ suffer from thirst or ˹the sun’s˺ heat.”

q: (to persuade Aadam ﵊ to eat from the tree,)
Shaytaan whispered to him saying, “O Aadam! Should I not show you the tree of eternity and a kingdom in which there is no
(He also swore that he is their well-wisher. Not knowing deceit, they believed him and ate from the tree.)
v.s: Then Satan whispered to him; he said, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that will not deteriorate?"
v.c: But Satan whispered to him, saying, “O Adam! Shall I show you the Tree of Immortality and a kingdom that does not fade away?”

q: (all their clothing disappeared, because of which)
their private parts became exposed to each other. They then started covering themselves with the leaves of Jannah. Aadam ﵊
broke the command of his Rabb and deviated
v.s: And they [i.e., Adam and his wife] ate of it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves from the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and erred.
v.c: So they both ate from the tree and then their nakedness was exposed to them, prompting them to cover themselves with leaves from Paradise. So Adam disobeyed his Lord, and ˹so˺ lost his way.

q: accepted his repentance and made him steadfast on guidance
v.s: Then his Lord chose him and turned to him in forgiveness and guided [him].
v.c: Then his Lord chose him ˹for His grace˺, accepted his repentance, and guided him ˹rightly˺.

q: to each other. When there come to you
then whoever will follow My guidance shall never go astray
v.s: [God] said, "Descend from it [i.e., Paradise] - all, [your descendants] being enemies to one another. And if there should come to you guidance from Me - then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter].
v.c: Allah said, “Descend, both of you, from here together ˹with Satan˺ as enemies to each other. Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray ˹in this life˺ nor suffer ˹in the next˺.

q: Whoever turns away from My advice
and We shall raise him blind on the Day of Qiyaamah
(after which his sight will be restored to see Jahannam).
v.s: And whoever turns away from My remembrance - indeed, he will have a depressed [i.e., difficult] life, and We will gather [i.e., raise] him on the Day of Resurrection blind."
v.c: But whoever turns away from My Reminder will certainly have a miserable life, then We will raise them up blind on the Day of Judgment.”

q: He will say, “O my Rabb! Why have you raised me blind when I was indeed one who could see?”
v.s: He will say, "My Lord, why have you raised me blind while I was [once] seeing?"
v.c: They will cry, “My Lord! Why have you raised me up blind, although I used to see?”

q: (is how it shall be for you).
Our Aayaat came to you, but you forgot them. In the same way
(and your request will not be heeded to).”
v.s: [God] will say, "Thus did Our signs come to you, and you forgot [i.e., disregarded] them; and thus will you this Day be forgotten."
v.c: Allah will respond, “It is so, just as Our revelations came to you and you neglected them, so Today you are neglected.”

q: Thus do We punish those who transgress
the limits and do not believe in the Aayaat
of their Rabb. The punishment of the Aakhirah is undoubtedly more severe and more lasting
(than the punishment of this world which comes to an end with death and of initial blindness).
v.s: And thus do We recompense he who transgressed and did not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring.
v.c: This is how We reward whoever transgresses and does not believe in the revelations of their Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe and more lasting.

q: not guided by the fact that We destroyed many nations before them, in whose localities
(can they not see that they may be destroyed for committing kufr just as those people were destroyed)?
in this for the intelligent ones.
v.s: Then, has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them as they walk among their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs for those of intelligence.
v.c: Is it not yet clear to them how many peoples We destroyed before them, whose ruins they still pass by? Surely in this are signs for people of sound judgment.

q: If it were not for a decree
that had already proceeded from your Rabb
(that these people will be punished in the Aakhirah),
v.s: And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it [i.e., punishment] would have been an obligation [due immediately], and [if not for] a specified term [decreed].
v.c: Had it not been for a prior decree from your Lord ˹O Prophet˺ and a term already set, their ˹instant˺ doom would have been inevitable.

q: say and glorify the praises of your Rabb before the rising of the sun
And glorify Him during the hours of the night
(by performing the Maghrib salaah and Isha salaah)
and at the ends of the day
(by performing the Zuhr salaah, which occurs at the end of the first part of the day and at the beginning of the second part of the day)
so that you become well pleased
v.s: So be patient over what they say and exalt [God] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting; and during periods of the night [exalt Him] and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied.
v.c: So be patient ˹O Prophet˺ with what they say. And glorify the praises of your Lord before sunrise and before sunset, and glorify Him in the hours of the night and at both ends of the day, so that you may be pleased ˹with the reward˺.

q: of the worldly life that We have granted groups of them
to enjoy as a test for them
(to see which of them will use these bounties for Allaah's obedience and which of them will use it to anger Allaah).
v.s: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have given enjoyment to [some] categories of them, [its being but] the splendor of worldly life by which We test them. And the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring.
v.c: Do not let your eyes crave what We have allowed some of the disbelievers to enjoy; the ˹fleeting˺ splendour of this worldly life, which We test them with. But your Lord’s provision ˹in the Hereafter˺ is far better and more lasting.

q: your family to perform salaah and
remain steadfast on it. We do not ask provision
from you, but We provide for you
(your duty is to perform your salaah and not to forsake it in search of sustenance because We shall provide it for you).
v.s: And enjoin prayer upon your family [and people] and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the [best] outcome is for [those of] righteousness.
v.c: Bid your people to pray, and be diligent in ˹observing˺ it. We do not ask you to provide. It is We Who provide for you. And the ultimate outcome is ˹only˺ for ˹the people of˺ righteousness.

q: (a miracle that we wish to see)
(to prove that he is Allaah's Rasool)?”
contained in the previous scriptures not reached them?

(Has Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Qur'aan not come to them, as was mentioned in the divine scriptures of the past Ambiyaa ﵊? Whereas the Qur'aan is ample proof that Rasulullaah ﷺ is really Allaah's Rasool, the Kuffaar still asked for other miracles because they did not want to believe him.)
v.s: And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the former scriptures?
v.c: They demand, “If only he could bring us a sign from his Lord!” Have they not ˹already˺ received a confirmation of what is in earlier Scriptures?

q: If We had to destroy them with a punishment before
“O our Rabb! Why did You not send a Rasool to us so that we could have followed Your Aayaat before being disgraced and humiliated
(by being made to enter Jahannam)?” (Therefore, Allaah had always sent Ambiyaa ﵊ and others to warn people of the consequences of rejecting Imaan.)
v.s: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before him, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could have followed Your verses [i.e., teachings] before we were humiliated and disgraced?"
v.c: Had We destroyed them with a torment before this ˹Prophet came˺, they would have surely argued, “Our Lord! If only You had sent us a messenger, we would have followed Your revelations before being humiliated and put to shame.”

q: is waiting, so you also wait
(to see whether it is you or we who will attain salvation).
you shall come to learn who are the people of the straight path and who are rightly guided ones
v.s: Say, "Each [of us] is waiting; so wait. For you will know who are the companions of the sound path and who is guided."
v.c: Say ˹to them, O Prophet˺, “Each ˹of us˺ is waiting, so keep waiting! You will soon know who is on the Straight Path and is ˹rightly˺ guided.”
